text.p: Australian has deported 92 Chinese boatpeople whose bid for asylum in Australia was rejected, acting Immigration Minister Amanda Vanstone said on Tuesday.
Vanstone said the would-be refugees had not met conditions set for granting asylum and had been returned to China overnight.
"The people had not engaged Australia's protection obligations and had exhausted all avenues to remain in Australia," she said in a statement.
The people -- who had arrived from China on five boats between 1992 and 1996 -- flew out on a charter flight from Port Hedland accompanied by Immigration Department officials.
After their inital applications were rejected most of them took their cases to review.
This enabled them to stay in Australia for some time under the country's lengthy legal processes for dealing with refugee applications.
Of the 232 asylum seekers in detention at the Port Hedland camp on the north-western coast of Australia, 158 are from China, a government immigration spokesman said.
